title: Averages, Mixtures & Alligation
relevance: Core quantitative aptitude for campus OAs and SDE screening; averages, mixtures, and alligation recur as direct and disguised word problems.

phases.goal: Establish the core formulas for average, weighted average, alligation, and repeated replacement.

must_hit.point: Average equals sum of observations divided by number of observations n; weighted average combines group sizes ni with averages Ai as (n1A1+n2A2+...)/(n1+n2+...).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both the simple mean and the weighted-average formula with ni and Ai.

must_hit.point: Alligation rule: quantity of cheaper over quantity of dearer equals (d-m)/(m-c) for cheaper price c, dearer price d, and mean price m.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the cheaper:dearer ratio as (d-m):(m-c) or (d-m)/(m-c).

must_hit.point: Repeated replacement: if V units of pure liquid have r units replaced by water n times, final pure amount is V(1-r/V)^n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recalls Final amount = V(1-r/V)^n with V, r, and n.

probes: State the formulas for weighted average, the alligation cheaper-to-dearer ratio, and repeated replacement of r from V done n times.

hints.1: Start from mean as sum over count, then how two priced lots combine around a mean price.
hints.2: Weighted average uses ni and Ai in numerator and denominator; alligation uses distances of c and d from m; replacement compounds the retained fraction.

phases.goal: Show how averages move when adding, replacing, or correcting values, and how alligation finds mix ratios from fractions.

must_hit.point: The average of consecutive terms in an arithmetic progression is the middle term.
must_hit.evidence_hint: With average 27 of 5 consecutive odd numbers, middle is 27 so sequence 23,25,27,29,31 and first×last=713.

must_hit.point: New value = old average + (increase in average × new number of elements).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Class of 30 at average 14 rises by 1 when teacher is included: teacher age = 14+(1×31)=45.

must_hit.point: When one wrong value is corrected, apply the net sum change divided by n rather than rebuilding the full sum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: 83 misread as 43 gives net +40 over 40 students, so average rises from 65 to 66.

must_hit.point: For concentration mixes, alligate on one component's fraction in each vessel against the target fraction.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Milk fractions 3/5 and 4/9 toward target 1/2 give vessel ratio 5:9.

probes: How do you find a new person's value when they raise the average, and how do you mix two milk-water vessels to get equal milk and water?

hints.1: An added person must cover the average lift for everyone now in the set; for mixes, pick milk fraction first.
hints.2: Use new value = old avg + (delta × new count); alligation distances are |d-m| and |m-c| on those fractions.
hints.3: Teacher: 14+(1×31)=45. Fractions 3/5 and 4/9 vs 1/2 → distances 1/18 and 1/10 → 5:9.

phases.goal: Separate cases where arithmetic mean is wrong from cases where alligation must use cost, not selling price.

must_hit.point: For equal distances at speeds x and y, average speed is 2xy/(x+y), not the arithmetic mean of the speeds.
Never apply alligation on selling price when profit is involved; first find the mean cost price on the same basis.
must_hit.evidence_hint: From SP 68.20 with 10% gain, mean CP=68.20/1.1=62, then alligation yields cheaper:dearer 3:2.

probes: Why is a round trip at 40 km/h and 60 km/h not average speed 50, and why is alligation on selling price wrong when there is profit?

hints.1: Average speed is weighted by time; profit changes which price alligation may use.
hints.2: Equal distance → 2xy/(x+y); convert SP to mean CP before alligation.

phases.goal: Apply replacement and alligation to OA-style mixture, alloy, and fraudulent-blend word problems.

must_hit.point: After n replacements of r from volume V, remaining original liquid is V(1-r/V)^n.
Alloy word problems reduce to alligation on gold fractions toward a 1/2 target.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gold fractions 7/9 and 7/18 vs 1/2 give A:B=2:5; of 70 kg total, Alloy B is 50 kg.

must_hit.point: Fraudulent blend: find the fair alligation ratio first, adjust after secret replacement of part of the dearer share, then recompute weighted cost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Fair blend of 12 and 28 around 20 is 1:1; after replacing 25% of the arabica share, actual CP is 18 /kg.

probes: 50 L milk with 5 L replaced by water three times—how much milk remains? How do you unwrap an alloy melt into alligation?

hints.1: Use the compounded retained-fraction formula; for alloys, convert each alloy ratio to a gold fraction.
hints.2: Final=V(1-r/V)^n; alligate each alloy's gold fraction against 1/2, then scale parts to total mass.
hints.3: 50(9/10)^3=36.45; A:B=2:5 so 5 of 7 parts of 70 kg is 50 kg Alloy B.

tradeoffs.topic: Arithmetic mean of speeds vs time-weighted average speed
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Average speed is weighted by time, not distance. For equal distances at x and y use 2xy/(x+y); (40+60)/2=50 is wrong and 48 km/h is correct.

tradeoffs.topic: Alligation on selling price vs cost price
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Alligation needs values on the same basis. With profit, convert SP to mean CP first (e.g. SP 68.20 at 10% profit → CP 62), then alligate on costs.

gotchas.trap: Treating average speed as the arithmetic mean of the two speeds on a round trip.
gotchas.correction: Speed is weighted by time; for equal distances use 2xy/(x+y).

gotchas.trap: Applying alligation directly on selling price when a profit percentage is given.
gotchas.correction: Find the mean cost price from SP and profit first, then alligate on costs.

gotchas.trap: Rebuilding the entire sum when one misread score is corrected.
gotchas.correction: Take the net change in sum and divide by n to get the change in average.
